title: How a visual is made
kicker: The visual skill · one topic, one printable page
status: SAMPLE · every block type in use
lede: A visual is a short illustrated page that explains one topic to a reader who was not in the conversation. The agent writes the content as data. A fixed template draws it, and a checker prints it to PDF and looks for problems before anyone sees it.
shows: The visual skill's pipeline, the data file, the PDF checks and what a run costs

sections.title: From a conversation to a page
sections.takeaway: The agent plans the page before it writes anything, and checks the PDF before it saves it.

steps.title: READ
steps.text: Find the topic in the conversation.

steps.title: GATHER
steps.text: Read the documents the topic rests on.

steps.title: PLAN
steps.text: Sections, the point of each, the picture in each.

steps.title: WRITE
steps.text: Fill the data file. No markup.

steps.title: CHECK
steps.text: Print to PDF, look, fix. Five tries at most.

steps.title: SAVE
steps.text: PDF and data file saved, index updated.

blocks.title: Why the plan is a gate
blocks.text: A page built on the wrong outline has to be rewritten, not fixed. The plan is short, so it is cheap to correct before the writing starts.

sections.title: Three files, three jobs
sections.takeaway: The agent only ever writes the data file. The template and the script never change for one page.

items.title: What the page says
items.text: Sections, takeaways, blocks. Kept in the visual's own folder with the PDF and a README, so the next edit is a data edit.

items.title: How it looks
items.text: One design for every visual. A new need is a change to the template, made once.

items.title: Whether it works
items.text: Checks the data, prints the PDF, measures margins and gaps, and updates the index.

sections.title: The building blocks
sections.takeaway: Pick the block by the job it does for the reader, not by how it looks.

rows: show parts and how they connect
compare amounts or show change over time
lead with two to four key numbers
set options side by side with a pick
group rules, flag a warning, define terms

children.label: blocks
children.note: one picture or more, with short text

sections.title: What the PDF check looks for
sections.takeaway: A script catches what can be measured. The agent looks at each changed page for the rest.

items: Text or borders in the margin
Blank pages and big empty gaps
A heading left alone at the foot of a page
Does each section make sense to a new reader?
Is every sentence plain and short?
Is every short form spelled out once?
Do the pictures match the words?

options.name: Save the PDF
options.verdict: When all checks pass within five tries.

options.name: Save the HTML
cons: Print layout depends on the browser
options.verdict: When the PDF still fails after five tries, or when asked.

sections.title: What a run costs
sections.takeaway: Most of the cost is reading the source documents and looking at the pages, not writing the data.

items.title: Topic named
items.text: First line of the reply says what the page is about.

items.title: Plan shown
items.text: Sections and pictures, as the default.

items.meaning: A small piece of text the model reads or writes; cost is counted in tokens.
One illustrated page about one topic, saved as a PDF or a single HTML file.
